context:
Goal: Swift screens follow the same layout standard as web screens (your 183 note).
What this is: rule ux-swift-same-intent says a Swift screen spaces its items from the parent stack (VStack(spacing:) and the like), never by padding one item to push its neighbour away, and uses shared spacing values that grow with text size (@ScaledMetric).
Problem (rule): no check holds the rule. home, degen and mailaudit break it; ios-adblock holds it. Two of its demands may ask for more than the outcome needs: every stack must set spacing (the platform's default gap is fine), and spacing must use @ScaledMetric tokens (no app does).
Based on (ruling): 183 note (11:22 CST Nov 6): send a lane to find out whether the rule is right to apply.
Based on (measured): lane ux-swift-same-intent-check scan, Nov 6: home 30 of 302 stacks set no spacing, degen 37 of 214, mailaudit 10 of 87, plus a padding push at native/Manifest/ItemLine.swift:90.
Departs from: main states the Swift rule with no check — a adds a check and narrows the rule; b files debts; c retires the section.

Not blocking: nothing waits on it.

options.gain: The rule asks only what matters (no padding that pushes a neighbour) and a check holds it in all 4 apps.
options.label: Narrow it and add a check
options.lose: A check to build, then one fix lane per app that breaks it.

options.label: Keep it as written, one debt per app
options.lose: The rule stays unenforced and asks for what no app does.

options.label: Retire the Swift section
options.lose: Swift screens have no layout standard; padding pushes go unflagged.

title: Swift layout rule: add a check and narrow it, file debts, or retire it?
why: Recommended: a. It keeps the intent you agreed to (the parent spaces its children) and drops the two demands that serve no one.
